title: Hochul, Blakeman rally supporters amid historic early voting turnout - ABC7 New York

 Hochul, Blakeman rally supporters amid historic early voting turnout 
 N.J. Burkett has the latest on New York's gubernatorial election. WABC By N.J. Burkett Friday, October 30, 2026 9:35PM Share NEW YORK (WABC) -- Gov. Kathy Hochul and Republican challenger Bruce Blakeman campaigned in supportive areas Friday as early voting continued across New York, with both candidates emphasizing affordability, taxes and voter turnout ahead of Election Day.
 Hochul addressed hundreds of sanitation workers at a union hall, where supporters cheered, chanted, and waved signs as part of a voter-turnout effort.
 "People are turning out to vote because they want to make sure that we don't get a crazy Trump guy in the governor's mansion in Albany. So that's why people are turning out right now," Hochul said.
 The governor began the day greeting commuters outside Atlantic Terminal in Brooklyn.
 "Our messaging is really, really resonating now as we talk to you about their greatest needs, which is affordability; they need more help dealing with the cost of everything," Hochul said.
 Blakeman spent part of Friday in Nassau County, where he participated in a ceremony swearing in 80 recruits to the Nassau County Police Department. He pointed to the county's crime rate and fiscal condition as key accomplishments.
 "Safest county in America. Budget surpluses of every budget. State comptroller saying our finances are excellent. I haven't raised taxes a penny in five years," Blakeman said.
 Blakeman also signed a pledge promising not to raise taxes if elected and challenged Hochul on affordability and tax issues.
 "This state is one of the least affordable states in the United States of America. Under Kathy Hochul, we're the highest tax state in America, the highest. It's a badge of shame," Blakeman said.
 Hundreds of thousands of New Yorkers have voted early statewide, reflecting strong engagement from voters backing their preferred candidates.
 "I think people are excited for change," one voter said.
 Another voter said early voting was simply part of a long-standing routine.
 "I don't know what it means about this year's elections, and I don't want to guess. I vote early every election cycle. It's just it's my habit," the voter said.
